pr.title: Reimplement DestinationPropagation according to live ranges.
pr.description:
This PR reimplements DestinationPropagation as a problem of merging live-ranges of locals. We merge locals that have disjoint live-ranges. This allows merging several locals in the same round by updating live range information.

Live ranges are mainly computed using the `MaybeLiveLocals` analysis. The subtlety is that we split each statement and terminator in 2 positions. The first position is the regular statement. The second position is a shadow, which is always more live. It encodes partial writes and dead writes as a local being live for half a statement. This half statement ensures that writes conflict with another local's writes and regular liveness.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: No source-grounded historical wrong transformation can be constructed for PR #145541. The PR reimplements DestinationPropagation as live-range union-find; the only changed regression expectations are optimization-quality/representative changes (`cycle` now merges into `_1` instead of `_6`; `dead_stores_*` now uses `_2` instead of `_3`) and are semantically equivalent MIR outputs. The PR text and diff never claim a semantic miscompile fix, and the sole nearby "miscompilation" reference (`nrvo_miscompile_111005`) is an unrelated RenameReturnPlace test that retains its FIXME. Modeling the old round-based representative choice as an "incorrect transformation" would only manufacture an arbitrary return-value difference, not a real wrong-code rewrite. Any valid program where both algorithms run would produce the same observed value, so a Miri-validated differing pair cannot be built without inventing an unrelated bug.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, DestinationPropagation collected copy-like assignment candidates, filtered them per basic block using whole-location MaybeLiveLocals plus a WriteInfo set of written locals, chose at most one destination per source per optimization round using a merged_locals set, unioned liveness rows for each selected merge, and repeated candidate collection/liveness filtering until no merges remained. Candidate endpoints were sorted and possibly swapped, and required source locals were skipped during candidate collection. This is the superseded algorithm, not a source-backed claim of a semantic miscompile.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical transformation to model: the old round-based merge could choose a different representative and could use a local in only one merge per round. In particular, for a statement such as `_6 = copy _1`, the old sorted/required-adjusted candidate pair could favor `_1 -> _6`, while the reimplementation records `(lhs, rhs)` and replaces lhs `_6` by rhs `_1`; the supplied cycle expectation changes from `debug y => _6` to `debug y => _1`. The old loop also postponed transitive/chain merges until later rounds. The evidence shows an optimization reimplementation and expected-MIR changes, not a demonstrated wrong-code rewrite; do not label the old output as a confirmed miscompile.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies for which DestinationPropagation is enabled (`mir_opt_level >= 3`). Candidate statements are `lhs = CopyForDeref(rhs)` or `lhs = Use(Copy(rhs) | Move(rhs))` where both sides are direct locals (`as_local`) with no projection. Candidates exclude address-taken/borrowed locals and, after unions, must not rename both required endpoints. Relevant cases include chains/cycles of locals, dead stores, partial writes such as SetDiscriminant, terminator reads/writes in Call or InlineAsm, return places/arguments, and both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR.
analysis.summary: This optimization PR replaces DestinationPropagation's round-based candidate filtering with union-find merging of locals whose MaybeLiveLocals live ranges are disjoint. Reusable correctness knowledge: compute liveness at two positions per statement/terminator (a normal position and a more-live shadow), mark all full/partial writes live in the shadow so dead and partial writes conflict, keep terminator operand reads live in the shadow so they conflict with that terminator's destination write, preserve required locals after unions, skip borrowed locals, and update both merged rows after each union so later disjointness checks see the merged range.
analysis.trigger: Merging two or more locals connected by copy/move assignments when their live ranges are disjoint at half-statement granularity; especially assignment chains/cycles, dead stores, partial writes, calls/inline asm, and required or borrowed locals.
preconditions: DestinationPropagation is enabled only at MIR optimization level 3 or higher: `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 3`.
Candidate statements are copy-like assignments `lhs = CopyForDeref(rhs)` or `lhs = Use(Copy(rhs) | Move(rhs))` where both `lhs` and `rhs` are direct locals.
Neither endpoint may be in the `borrowed` set (address-taken locals are not merged).
The merged locals must have disjoint half-statement live ranges after accounting for previous unions.
At least one endpoint must be renameable: the return place and function arguments are required and cannot be renamed; if both are required the merge is skipped.
Candidate collection may happen before liveness is computed, but required-local checks must happen after union-find lookup because one non-required local may unify with several required locals.
pitfalls: Do not use a single whole-statement live point for writes: dead writes then have an empty range and can incorrectly appear disjoint from another local. Mark Def and PartialWrite locals live at the shadow/after position.
Do not treat PartialWrite as NonUse, and do not treat it as a full Def. In this patch SetDiscriminant on a non-indirect place becomes PartialWrite; dereferences remain uses of the base local.

For terminators, operands read by a call must also be live at the shadow position: an argument may be read after the destination has been written, so the read must conflict with the destination write.

Required locals must be checked only after transitive unions. Prefer renaming a non-required local into a required one; skip only when both endpoints are required. Swapping the merge direction is required when the current source is required and the destination is not.
After a union, union both old source and destination live rows into the new head row. Otherwise later disjointness decisions use stale ranges and can permit an unsafe merge.
`Operand::Move` is not read-only. The old source comment records that a previous version treated Move as read-only and that this was unsound; keep move sources conservatively involved in conflicts.
Do not infer that the `nrvo_miscompile_111005` test validates DestinationPropagation: it is a `RenameReturnPlace` test and retains a FIXME for an already-known wrong output.
Downstream expected-MIR changes such as `let mut _3` becoming `let _3` can be consequences of removed writes/renaming, not separate correctness guarantees.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused `tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/` MIR tests with `//@ test-mir-pass: DestinationPropagation` and both panic strategies. Build custom-MIR chains/cycles where all candidates have disjoint ranges: assert the selected representative and that copy assignments become nops; the supplied cycle test demonstrates the representative change from `_6` to `_1`. Add dead-store cases where a local is written, overwritten, then restored; assert the expected `debug b => _2` and `_2 = copy _1` / `_1 = move _2` output, ensuring dead writes still occupy a shadow position. Add same-statement partial-write and call/inline-asm read/write cases to verify conflicts. Add required-local cases (return place/argument plus non-required temporary) and both-required cases, plus an address-taken local. For differential testing, construct pairs of MIR bodies identical except for a dead/partial write or a terminator read, so only the conflict/live-range condition changes; do not use the unrelated RenameReturnPlace miscompile test as evidence about DestinationPropagation.
